name: Iron hydroxide polymaltose complex
drafted_by: AI-assisted draft (Claude) for review by Dr. W. Rivero
summary: Iron(III) hydroxide polymaltose complex is an oral iron whose absorbed iron is handled by normal iron metabolism, not the kidneys; unabsorbed iron leaves in feces. The Swedish label has very limited data in kidney impairment and gives no dose adjustment. It has no US FDA label.
kidney_function_basis: Not renally cleared; the SmPC gives no kidney grading. Bands shown on creatinine clearance (CrCl).

bands.recommendation: Iron deficiency (adults and adolescents over 12): 100 to 300 mg iron daily (1 to 3 chewable tablets), once or in divided doses, with or after meals; guide by hemoglobin and iron stores (SmPC).
Very limited data in kidney impairment; no dose adjustment given (SmPC). Iron is not renally cleared. Use with caution and specialist judgment.

monitoring: Hemoglobin, ferritin and transferrin saturation to guide dose and duration (SmPC 4.2). Do not combine with parenteral iron.

pediatric.approved_ages: Chewable tablets: over 12 years; younger children should use the drops (SmPC).

renal.recommendation: Tablets not for children 12 and under; no pediatric kidney data.
